newsitem.title: USA: Sony says PlayStation sales far from peaking.
newsitem.headline: Sony says PlayStation sales far from peaking.

text.p: Sony Corp. said Thursday it expects PlayStation, the hot-selling video-game console, to have strong sales and said that even with a shipment of 6 million units this year, it may not be able to meet retail demand.
PlayStation has been on the market for three years.

"This year, we are looking to bring in 6 million PlayStation units into the United States," said Kazuo Hirai, chief operating officer of Sony Computer Entertainment, the Sony arm that makes PlayStation. That will more than double the number of PlayStations in North America to about 11 million.
Even a shipment of 6 million units may not be enough to meet demand this year. U.S. retailers have told Sony they could need 9 million units, Sony executives said.
Sony could sell even a bigger number of PlayStations in 1998, said Jack Tretton, Sony Computer Entertainment vice president of sales.

Sony entered the video game console business in 1995, taking on industry giants Nintendo Co. and Sega Enterprises Ltd. Its PlayStation was among the first machines to use a new generation of microprocessors that can handle more realistic graphics.

Partly helped by an early launch and a software library of more than 800 titles, Sony leads in the number of next-generation consoles. By its own count Sony has sold 17 million PlayStations worldwide, compared with 6 million Nintendo 64s and 9 million Sega Saturns.

At the Electronic Entertainment Expo being held in Atlanta this week, Sony and other software companies previewed more than 150 new PlayStation games, slated to be released in time for the Christmas shopping season.
